sentences.text:
The petitioners herein have sought quashing of FIR No. 87 of 2019 registered at Vinoba Bhave Police Station, Mumbai, for offences under Sections 498A, 324, 323, 504 and 506 r/w 34 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC).
3.
Petitioner No. 1 is the husband of respondent No. 2, petitioner No. 2 was the mother-in-law of respondent No. 2 who expired during Rushikesh 17 WP.2561.2019.doc
the pendency of this petition,
petitioner No. 3 is the sister-in-law of respondent No. 2 and petitioner No. 4 is the daughter of petitioner No. 3.

4. A joint affidavit of the petitioner No. 1 and respondent No. 2 dated 17th December 2025 is also placed on record, wherein it is stated that they are residing together and all the disputes and misunderstandings between them have been resolved by the intervention of elders.

It is specifically stated that both of them are living peacefully with each other, and during the pendency of this petition, the respondent No. 2 give birth to a girl child and that the petitioner No. 1 and respondent No. 2 are jointly taking care of their children.
5. The petitioner No. 1 and respondent No. 2 are present in Court.
Respondent No. 2 is identified by the advocate on record appearing for her.

6. By way of amendment, the petitioners have also prayed for quashing of the chargesheet as well as Criminal Case bearing No. PW/5901448 of 2019, pending before the Court of Judicial Magistrate First Class, 59th Court, Kurla, Mumbai.

In such cases when the disputes between the parties are resolved, such affidavits are placed on record seeking quashing of the criminal proceedings by Rushikesh 17 WP.2561.2019.doc consent.

8. In the case of Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab 1 the Supreme Court considered the question as to whether non-comboundable offences could be quashed by the High Court in such circumstances where the criminal proceedings would not lead to any conclusion and the ends of justice would be met by allowing such petitions.

entities.text: Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In paragraph 61 of the said judgment, it is held as follows:
"61.

The position that emerges from the above discussion can be summarised thus:
the power of the High Court in quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR or complaint in exercise of its inherent jurisdiction is distinct and different from the power given to a criminal court for compounding the offences under Section 320 of the Code.

Inherent power is of wide plenitude with no statutory limitation but it has to be exercised in accord with the guideline engrafted in such power viz. : (i) to secure the ends of justice, or (ii) to prevent abuse of the process of any court.

In what cases power to quash the criminal proceeding or complaint or FIR may be exercised where the offender and the victim have settled their dispute would depend on the facts and circumstances of each case and no category can be prescribed.

However, before Dhruplal Ramnarayan Agrahari And Ors. vs The State Of Maharasthra And Anr. on 22 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70176315/
2 exercise of such power, the High Court must have due regard to the nature and gravity of the crime.

entities.text: Dhruplal Ramnarayan Agrahari And Ors. vs The State Of Maharasthra And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Heinous and serious offences of mental depravity or offences like murder, rape, dacoity, etc. cannot be fittingly quashed even though the victim or victim's family and the offender have settled the dispute.
Such offences are not private in nature and have a serious impact on society.

Similarly, any compromise between the victim and the offender in relation to the offences under special statutes like the Prevention of Corruption Act or the offences committed by public servants while working in that capacity, etc.; cannot provide for any basis for quashing criminal 1 (2012) 10 SCC 303 Rushikesh 17 WP.2561.2019.doc proceedings involving such offences.

But the criminal cases having overwhelmingly and predominatingly civil flavour stand on a different footing for the purposes of quashing, particularly the offences arising from commercial, financial, mercantile, civil, partnership or such like transactions or the offences arising out of matrimony relating to dowry, etc. or the family disputes where the wrong is basically private or personal in nature and the parties have resolved their entire dispute.

In this category of cases, the High Court may quash the criminal proceedings if in its view, because of the compromise between the offender and the victim, the possibility of conviction is remote and bleak and continuation of the criminal case would put the accused to great oppression and prejudice and extreme injustice would be caused to him by not quashing the criminal case despite full and complete settlement and compromise with the victim.

In other words, the High Court must consider whether it would be unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to continue with the criminal proceeding or continuation of the criminal proceeding would tantamount to abuse of process of law despite settlement and compromise between the victim and the wrongdoer and whether to secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that the criminal case is put to an end and if the answer to the above question(s) is in the affirmative, the High Court shall be well within its jurisdiction to quash the criminal proceeding."

9. We are satisfied that the said position of law applies to the facts of the present case and hence we are inclined to allow the petition with the consent of respondent No. 2.
10.
In view of the above, the petition is allowed.

Consequently, FIR No. 87 of 2019 dated 6th April 2019, registered at Vinoba Bhave Nagar Police Station, Kurla, Mumbai, along with chargesheet filed in pursuance thereof, and Criminal Case bearing No. PW/5901448 of Rushikesh 17 WP.2561.2019.doc 2019, pending before the Judicial Magistrate First Class, 59 th Court, Kurla,
Mumbai, are quashed.
